items.stem: A particle has velocity v = −6t² + 42t − 60 m s⁻¹. Aisha says the particle is at rest at t = 7/2 because the acceleration is zero then. Explain the error.
items.answer: a = 0 at t = 7/2 means the velocity is stationary (here the greatest velocity, 27/2 m s⁻¹), not zero; it is at rest when v = 0, at t = 2 and t = 5.
items.markingKey: B1 a = 0 gives stationary velocity; B1 at rest when v = 0 [2]

items.stem: A particle has velocity v = −t² + 5t − 4 m s⁻¹. Priya uses v = u + at to find the acceleration over the first 4 s. Explain why this does not give the acceleration at t = 4.
items.answer: The acceleration varies (a = −2t + 5), so (v − u)/t gives only an average; at t = 4 the acceleration is −3 m s⁻².
items.markingKey: B1 acceleration not constant; B1 differentiates to find a at t [2]
